question.problem:
Consider the polar curve $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{3}⁡\theta $ for $\theta \in [0,\pi ).$ Given that 

$$
{x}^{′}(\theta )={cos}^{3}⁡\theta \,(5{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -4),\,{y}^{′}(\theta )=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta (5{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -3),
$$

and ${x}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=0,$ which of the following statements are true?

I. ${y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=0$

II. ${lim}_{\theta \to \pi /2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=0$

III. The curve has a horizontal tangent at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{2}$

*Hint: It is not necessary to use L'Hopital's rule to evaluate the limit in part II.*

choices.value: None of the statements are true
